home.title: PC checkup
home.subtitle: Find out what's slowing your PC down or filling it up, in plain words, and fix it in a click.
home.admin_banner: Some Windows system items (update cache, system temp files) need administrator rights.
home.empty_hint: Click Start checkup to see what needs attention. The checkup only looks; it never deletes anything.
home.verdict_good: Your PC is in good shape
home.summary: {count} things found · {size} can be freed safely
home.summary_clean: Nothing needs your attention right now.
home.findings_empty: The results of the checkup will appear here.
home.promise_body: OpenSweep never deletes your documents, photos, videos, downloads, chat history, game saves, passwords or browser logins. It only removes things programs can recreate, and always shows you the list first.
home.f_junk: {size} of junk files can be removed safely
home.f_junk_d: Temporary files, caches and update leftovers. Programs recreate them when needed, so deleting them has no downside.
home.f_junk_blocked: Another {size} in {count} items waits until you close the apps using it.
home.f_review_d: Package caches, the Recycle Bin and similar. Safe to delete, but you may want some of them, so they are never cleaned automatically.
home.f_ai_d: Downloaded models can be downloaded again. Delete the ones you no longer use.
home.f_disk_sys: Drive {drive} is almost full: {free} free of {total}
home.f_disk_sys_d: When the Windows drive fills up, the PC slows down and updates fail. Clean junk first, then see what else takes space in Disk map.
home.f_disk: Drive {drive} is almost full: {free} free of {total}
home.f_disk_d: Use Disk map to see which folders and files take the most space.
home.f_startup: {count} apps start with Windows but don't need to
home.f_startup_d: {names}. They slow down start-up and use memory in the background. Turning them off doesn't uninstall anything.
home.f_startup_ok: Startup looks fine ({count} apps start with Windows)
home.f_broken: {count} startup entries point to programs that no longer exist
home.f_broken_d: Leftovers from uninstalled software. Removing them is safe.
home.f_unused_d: {names}. If you don't need them any more, uninstall them.
home.f_memory_d: Programs running in the background use {size}: {names}. Close the ones you don't need.
home.plan_junk: Delete {size} of temporary files and caches
home.plan_startup: Stop {count} unnecessary apps from starting with Windows
home.plan_broken: Remove {count} startup entries whose program is gone
home.plan_safe: Your files, chats, logins and installed programs are not touched. Temporary files can't be brought back (programs recreate them), but startup changes can be undone with one click.
confirm.title: Confirm cleanup
confirm.permanent: Caches and temporary files are deleted permanently. Files that are in use are skipped.
confirm.recycle: Items marked "Review" are moved to the Recycle Bin so you can restore them.
confirm.recycle_off: Items marked "Review" are deleted permanently (you turned off the Recycle Bin in Settings).
confirm.no_undo: Emptying the Recycle Bin and removing Ollama models cannot be undone.
confirm.hint: Check the list below. Only these items will be touched.
done.title: Cleanup finished
done.recycled: {size} moved to the Recycle Bin. Empty it to free that space.
done.in_use: {count} files were in use and were skipped.
done.verdict_mostly: Mostly clean – a few files couldn't be removed yet
done.left_in_use: {count} files are being used by a program right now. Close your programs or restart the PC, then clean again to remove them.
done.left_recycled: {size} is in the Recycle Bin. Empty it to actually free that space.
done.left_running: {size} was skipped because these apps are open: {apps}. Close them and clean again.
done.left_admin: {size} of Windows system junk needs administrator rights. Restart OpenSweep as administrator to clean it.
done.left_review: {size} of items that need your decision (AI models, Recycle Bin…) were not touched. You can review them in Junk files.
clean.title: Junk files
clean.desc: Everything OpenSweep found, grouped by type. "Safe" items are recreated automatically; check "Review" items yourself.
ai.title: AI models & caches
ai.desc: Models are large but can be downloaded again. Each one is listed separately; only tick the ones you no longer use.
software.title: Programs
software.desc: Remove programs you no longer use, including ones Windows has forgotten about.
software.confirm:
Uninstall {name}?

The program's own uninstaller will open. Follow its steps.
software.waiting: Waiting for the uninstaller of {name} to finish…
software.failed: Could not start the uninstaller of {name}.
software.still_installed: {name} still seems to be installed. The uninstaller may have been cancelled or may still be running; click Refresh when it is done.
software.removed: {name} was removed. No leftover folders were found.
software.leftovers_body: {name} was removed, but these folders are still there. Ticked folders will be moved to the Recycle Bin.
software.leftovers_done: Leftover folders were moved to the Recycle Bin.
software.summary: {count} programs haven't been used for over {days} days. Together they take {size}.
software.reason_unused: Windows records show this program was last opened {days} days ago. If you no longer need it, uninstall it to free its space.
software.reason_no_record: Windows has no record of this program being opened. It may be unused, or it may only run in the background (drivers, services, helpers). Check before uninstalling.
software.reason_new: Installed less than a month ago.
software.reason_recent: Used {days} days ago, so you probably still need it.
software.pick: Select a program to see its details and whether you still use it.
software.reason_component: This is a runtime, driver or SDK. Other programs use it in the background, so it never shows as "opened". Keep it unless you know nothing needs it.
software.reason_today: Used today, so you probably still need it.
startup.title: Startup apps
startup.desc: Apps that start with Windows slow down boot and use memory all day. Each one gets a recommendation; turning one off never uninstalls it.
startup.needs_admin: Changing apps for all users needs administrator rights.
startup.stat_broken_hint: the program they start was deleted
startup.pick: Select an app to see what it is and whether it needs to start with Windows.
startup.why_security: Security software. It has to start with Windows to protect you. Keep it on.
startup.why_input: Input method. Without it you may not be able to type in your language. Keep it on.
startup.why_driver: Part of a hardware driver (sound, graphics, touchpad, keyboard keys…). Turning it off may break that hardware's extra features.
startup.why_system: Part of Windows. Keep it on.
startup.why_sync: File sync (cloud drive). Keep it on if you want your files synced all the time; otherwise open it when you need it.
startup.why_chat: Chat app. Keep it on if you want messages as soon as the PC starts; otherwise open it yourself.
startup.why_remote: Remote control software. Only needed at start-up if others connect to this PC when you're away.
startup.why_tool: A utility. Keep it if you use it every day.
startup.why_updater: Update checker. The program still updates itself when you open it, so it doesn't need to run all the time.
startup.why_cloud: Cloud drive or download manager. It uses memory and bandwidth in the background; open it when you want to download.
startup.why_game: Game launcher, booster or emulator. You can open it when you want to play.
startup.why_media: Video, music or social app. There's no need for it to start with Windows.
startup.why_browser: Browser or browser helper. Opening the browser yourself is enough.
startup.why_unknown: OpenSweep doesn't know this app. If you don't recognise it and don't use it, turning it off is safe; you can turn it back on later.
startup.why_broken: The program this entry starts was deleted, so it does nothing except leave an error behind. Removing it is safe.
startup.apply_confirm: Stop these {count} apps from starting with Windows?
startup.apply_undo: Nothing is uninstalled. Entries are backed up and can be restored by ticking them in OpenSweep. An app can have other startup sources.
startup.applied: Turned off {count} startup entries. Running programs remain open; check other sources of the same app separately.
startup.remove_confirm: Remove these startup entries? The programs they point to no longer exist. A backup is saved in the OpenSweep folder.
startup.task_note: This starts through Windows Task Scheduler (often at logon or every day), which is why it doesn't show up in Task Manager's startup list. Turning it off disables the task; you can turn it back on here.
startup.service_note: Turning this off disables the service, including manual starts; features that depend on it may be unavailable. Tick it again to restore its previous start mode. Administrator rights are required. A running service is not stopped.
startup.why_opensweep: OpenSweep's startup guard: it keeps the apps you turned off from turning themselves back on.
memory.title: Memory
memory.why_title: Why there is no "free RAM" button
memory.why_body: Windows already uses spare memory as a cache and hands it back instantly when an app needs it. "RAM cleaners" only force that data out, so it has to be read from disk again and your PC gets slower. What really helps is closing apps you are not using and turning off startup apps you don't need.
memory.critical: {name} is part of Windows and cannot be closed here.
memory.confirm:
Close {name}?

Unsaved work in this app will be lost.
memory.close_failed: Could not close {name}. It may need administrator rights.
memory.desc: See which apps use your memory, and which ones only run in the background.
memory.level_high: Memory is almost full – things will slow down
memory.tip_background: Programs running in the background use {size}: {names}. If you're not using them, close them, and turn off their startup so they don't come back.
memory.tip_apps: Close apps or browser tabs you're not using. If memory is often full, adding more RAM helps more than any cleaner.
memory.tip_ok: Nothing to do right now. Free memory is used by Windows as a speed-up cache, so it's normal for usage to look high.
memory.pick: Select an app to see what it is and whether it's worth closing.
memory.why_app: An app you have open. Close it from its own window to keep your work; use "Close app" only if it doesn't respond.
memory.why_background: Runs in the background without a window. Many are updaters, helpers or tray icons you don't need. Closing it is usually safe; it may start again on the next boot if it's a startup app.
memory.why_system: Part of Windows. It can't be closed here, and it shouldn't be.
memory.startup_hint: It also starts with Windows. Turning that off stops it from using memory after every boot.
memory.startup_disabled: Turned off matching startup entries for {name}; check other sources separately.
settings.title: Settings
settings.restart_needed: Restart OpenSweep to use the new language.
settings.recycle: Move items that need your decision to the Recycle Bin instead of deleting them
settings.recycle_hint: Safer, because you can put them back. The space is only freed after you empty the Recycle Bin. Items marked "Safe" (caches and temporary files) are always deleted right away, because programs recreate them.
settings.rules_hint: Most people can ignore this. If you know a program OpenSweep doesn't, you can add your own rule file to clean its folders.
settings.rule_errors: {count} problems were found in rule files:
settings.about_text: OpenSweep {version}. Free and open source (MIT license). No ads, no upsells, no telemetry. It only goes online when you check for updates.
settings.check_updates_auto: Check for a new version when OpenSweep starts (the only time it goes online by itself)
settings.update_failed: Couldn't check for updates. Check your internet connection, or visit the project website.
settings.update_available: OpenSweep {version} is available (you have {current}). Open the download page?
settings.theme_hint: Pick the look you like. Switching reloads the window; scan results need to be refreshed.
detail.pick: Select an item on the left to see exactly what is inside it.
detail.kept_value: Files newer than {days} day(s) are not deleted
detail.recycle_bin: {count} items are in the Recycle Bin. Open the Recycle Bin on the desktop to see them.
detail.ollama: This model is made of the data blocks below. Blocks shared with other models are kept.
folders.intro: These folders contain programs that are not registered in Windows, so you won't find them in Settings > Apps: unzipped "portable" programs, or folders left behind after an uninstall. Check each one before deleting.
folders.pick: Select a folder to see what is in it.
folders.not_scanned: Click Find to look for unlisted programs on all drives.
folders.running_hint: {apps} from this folder is running, so it can't be deleted. Close it first.
folders.reason_portable: Contains a program that was never installed through Windows (for example, it was just unzipped here). Deleting the folder removes the program; its settings elsewhere stay.
folders.reason_leftover: This folder is in a program folder but has no program in it any more. It is usually what's left after an uninstall.
folders.delete_body: Everything in this folder will be removed. Make sure there are no files of your own in it.
folders.delete_recycle: Move to the Recycle Bin (can be restored, but space is only freed after you empty it)
folders.deleted_recycle: {name} was moved to the Recycle Bin.
disk.title: Disk map
disk.desc: See what fills your drive. Bigger boxes take more space; the colour tells you whether it's safe to remove.
disk.empty: Pick a drive to see what takes up its space. Nothing is changed while analyzing.
disk.scan_hint: A full drive can take a minute or two.
disk.summary: {size} in {files} files and {folders} folders · analyzed in {seconds} s.
disk.denied: {count} folders couldn't be read (run as administrator to include them).
disk.pick: Click a box to see what it is. Double-click a folder to look inside.
disk.pick_file: Select a file to see what it is and whether you can delete it.
disk.types_hint: Click a type to list its largest files.
disk.recycle_confirm: Move "{name}" ({size}) to the Recycle Bin? You can restore it from there. Space is freed once you empty the Recycle Bin.
disk.recycled: "{name}" ({size}) was moved to the Recycle Bin.
disk.t_video: A video. Old recordings and downloaded videos are often the biggest files on a PC. If you don't need it, move it to an external drive or delete it.
disk.t_image: A picture. Keep your photos; consider backing them up before deleting anything.
disk.t_audio: Music or audio. Delete only if you no longer listen to it.
disk.t_document: A document. These are usually your own files – keep them.
disk.t_archive: A compressed file (zip, rar…). Often a download that was already unpacked – if so, the archive itself can go.
disk.t_installer: A program or installer. Installers you already ran (setup files in Downloads) can be deleted; programs inside Program Files should be uninstalled instead.
disk.t_diskimage: A disk image (system ISO, virtual machine disk, backup image). ISO files you already installed from can usually be deleted; virtual machine disks hold whole systems.
disk.t_model: An AI model file. It can usually be downloaded again. Use AI models & caches to remove whole models safely.
disk.t_program: Part of an installed program. Don't delete it by hand – uninstall the program instead.
disk.t_cache: Temporary file or log. Usually safe to remove – use Junk files to do it safely.
disk.t_other: OpenSweep can't tell what this file is for. If you don't recognise it, leave it alone.
disk.k_pagefile: Windows' virtual memory (page file). Windows needs it; never delete it. You can make it smaller or move it to another drive in System > About > Advanced system settings > Performance.
disk.k_hiberfil: Hibernation file. It's about as big as part of your memory. If you never use hibernate, run "powercfg -h off" as administrator and it disappears; don't delete it by hand.
disk.k_swapfile: Part of Windows' memory system. Leave it alone.
disk.k_winsxs: Windows component store. It looks huge because files are counted twice (they're shared with the Windows folder). Never delete from it; Windows' own Disk Cleanup can trim it.
disk.k_installer: Installer cache. Deleting from here breaks uninstalling and updating your programs. Don't touch it.
disk.k_updates: Windows Update downloads. Safe to clean with OpenSweep (Junk files).
disk.k_windows_temp: Windows' temporary files. Safe to clean with OpenSweep.
disk.k_windows: Windows itself. Don't delete anything here by hand. The parts that can be cleaned (updates, temp files) are in Junk files.
disk.k_windows_old: Your previous Windows version, kept after an upgrade. Remove it in Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files; afterwards you can't roll back.
disk.k_restore: System Restore points. Adjust how much space they may use in System Properties > System Protection; don't delete them by hand.
disk.k_recycle: The Recycle Bin. Files here still take space until you empty it.
disk.k_recovery: Files Windows needs to start up or repair itself. Don't touch.
disk.k_temp: Temporary files. Safe to clean with OpenSweep.
disk.k_ai_cache: Downloaded AI models. They can be downloaded again; remove the ones you don't use in AI models & caches.
disk.k_dev_cache: Caches of developer tools (pip, npm, Gradle…). They are rebuilt when needed; clean them in Junk files.
disk.k_browser_data: Browser profile: history, logins, extensions and cache. Don't delete it by hand or you'll lose your logins; the cache part can be cleaned in Junk files.
disk.k_wsl: Linux (WSL) or Docker virtual disks. They only grow; shrink them with the tools of WSL/Docker, never by deleting files.
disk.k_store_apps: Apps from the Microsoft Store and their data. Uninstall apps in Windows Settings > Apps rather than deleting folders.
disk.k_programs: Installed programs. To free space here, uninstall programs you don't use in Programs – deleting folders breaks them.
disk.k_programdata: Data shared by programs for all users (settings, licences, databases). Don't delete whole folders here.
disk.k_chat: Chat history and files you received (WeChat, QQ…). Clean it with the chat app's own storage manager so you choose what to keep.
disk.k_games: Installed games. Uninstall games you no longer play from their launcher (Steam, WeGame, Epic…).
disk.k_downloads: Your Downloads folder. It often collects installers and archives you no longer need – check the largest files.
disk.k_user_files: Your own files (documents, desktop, pictures, videos, music). OpenSweep never touches them. If they're too big, move some to another drive or the cloud.
disk.k_appdata_local: Data and caches programs keep for you (AppData\Local). Don't delete whole folders; the safe caches are listed in Junk files.
disk.k_appdata_roaming: Program settings and data (AppData\Roaming). Deleting folders here resets or breaks programs.
disk.k_appdata: Hidden folder where programs keep their data and caches. Don't delete it; clean the safe parts in Junk files.
disk.k_profile: Your user folder: your files plus program data. Look inside to see what's big.
disk.k_users: The folders of every user on this PC.
disk.k_small: Many small files, grouped together so the map stays readable.
disk.k_unreadable: Space used by system files OpenSweep can't read (restore points, protected system areas) or by folders without permission. Run as administrator to see more.
disk.k_unknown: OpenSweep doesn't recognise this folder. Look inside to see what's big. If you don't know what it is, don't delete it.
feedback.wrong_tip: Opens a pre-filled report in your browser. You can review and edit it before sending; your user name is removed.
errors.unexpected: Something went wrong. The details were saved to the error log (Settings → Open cleanup log).
theme.fresh_d: Bright and friendly. Follows Windows light/dark.
theme.fluent_d: Looks like Windows Settings. Follows light/dark.
guard.title: Startup guard
guard.on_text: Watching {count} startup programs you turned off. If one turns itself back on, OpenSweep switches it off again when you sign in or open it. It can't stop a program that has already started.
guard.off_text: Off. Programs you turn off may quietly turn themselves back on.
guard.came_back: {count} entries need disabling again or stronger blocking: {names}. Some require administrator rights.
guard.history_intro: These startup entries were disabled again or strengthened. This does not mean running programs were stopped:
guard.need_admin_restart: Some of these can only be turned off with administrator rights. Restart OpenSweep as administrator?
guard.home_fixed: Disabled again or strengthened {count} startup entries: {names}.
guard.home_admin: {count} apps turned their startup back on ({names}); turning them off needs administrator rights.
guard.notice_fixed: Disabled again or strengthened these entries: {names}.
guard.notice_admin_title: {count} apps turned their startup back on
guard.notice_admin: {names}. Click to open OpenSweep and turn them off.
guard.entry_note: This is OpenSweep's own startup guard. It runs for about a second at logon, switches back off any app that sneaked into startup, and exits; it does not stay running. Turn it off with the Startup guard switch at the top of this page.
boot.title: Startup diagnostic
boot.intro: Windows booted at {when}; {count} programs are visible now. This is a live snapshot including manual launches. Exited programs are unavailable; a path match does not prove a launch source.
boot.v_on: Matching entry {entry} is enabled now; this does not prove it launched the program.
boot.v_off: Matching entry {entry} is off now; parent: {parent}. It may have started before the change or through another source.
boot.v_off_gone: Matching entry {entry} is off now. The original parent is unavailable; the launch source is unknown.
boot.v_via_on: Parent: {parent}. Its matching entry {entry} is enabled now.
boot.v_via_off: Parent: {parent}. Its matching entry {entry} is off now; it may have started before the change.
boot.v_service: The parent chain includes the Windows service manager. Check the corresponding service.
boot.v_other: Parent: {parent}. No definite startup entry matched.
boot.v_other_gone: The original parent is unavailable; the launch source is unknown.
boot.failed: Could not read diagnostic data. Retry or run as administrator.
boot.partial: Some startup sources could not be read. See the report for details.
startup.restart_note: When this is on, Windows reopens the apps that were open when you restarted or signed out, even if their own startup entry is off. Turn it off to stop that. You can turn it back on any time.
startup.off_all_confirm: Turn off {count} startup entries? Windows components and OpenSweep itself are kept. You can turn any of them back on later.
disk.k_package_cache: Installer files that Windows programs (Visual Studio, .NET, Python, Office…) keep so they can repair, update or uninstall later. Deleting them can make those programs fail to update or uninstall. Leave it unless the programs are already gone.
disk.k_node_modules: Libraries downloaded for a JavaScript project. They can be downloaded again with npm or pnpm, so it's usually fine to delete them in projects you're not working on, but the project needs a reinstall before it runs again.
disk.k_git: A project's version history (Git). Deleting it erases that history; the project's working files stay.
disk.k_pycache: Python's precompiled cache. It is rebuilt automatically and safe to delete, but it saves very little space.
disk.k_venv: A Python virtual environment: the packages one project uses. It can be recreated from the project's requirements, but the project won't run until you do.
disk.k_driver_extract: Files a graphics or hardware driver installer unpacked here. Usually safe to remove once the driver is installed, but if you're unsure, leave it.
disk.id_program: Belongs to the installed program “{who}”. To free its space, uninstall the program instead of deleting files by hand.
disk.id_data_of: Looks like data kept by “{who}”: settings, caches or saved content. This is matched by name, so it's a good guess, not a certainty. Deleting it can reset that program.
disk.id_exe_folder: Contains {who}. It isn't linked to a program in your installed list, so it may be a portable, bundled or leftover program.
disk.id_windows: Holds Microsoft software ({who}), part of Windows or a Microsoft product. Leave it alone.
home.quick: Make my PC faster in one click
home.undo_text: Turned off {count} startup programs. Changed your mind?
home.undo_done: Done. {count} startup programs were turned back on.
done.equiv: That's about {photos} phone photos' worth of space.
disk.wins_title: Start here: the biggest things that are safe to clean
startup.legend: Orange = we suggest turning it off. Grey = your choice. Green = needed or harmless, keep it. Nothing is deleted; you can turn any of them back on.
welcome.title: Welcome to OpenSweep
welcome.intro: It finds what is slowing your PC down or filling your drives, explains each thing in plain words, and only changes anything after you say yes.
welcome.step1: Press the big button. OpenSweep checks your PC (about a minute).
welcome.step2: It shows you exactly what it would do. Nothing happens until you confirm.
welcome.step3: Startup changes can be undone with one click. Your documents, photos, chats and logins are never touched.
welcome.guard: Keep the apps I turn off from sneaking back into startup (recommended)
welcome.guard_hint: Some apps turn their own startup back on after updates. This checks once when you sign in and switches them off again. It does not keep running.
